speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for bringing me in. To properly evaluate the skin condition on your left dorsal hand, can you tell me when you first noticed this and if the area is itchy, painful, or oozing?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Understood, patient. Given your age, history of diabetes, and recent sunbathing, are the lesions on your left dorsal hand raised, scaly, or crusted, and did they appear shortly after your outdoor activities?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis

The description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with a history of sun exposure is highly characteristic of Actinic Keratosis. Given your lack of pain or tenderness, this aligns well with a premalignant lesion rather than an infected or inflammatory condition. Do you have any history of other skin cancers or a family history of basal cell carcinoma?
